llm.summary: The skill largely implements a stock assistant as described, but there are clear mismatches between what it declares and what it actually does — notably undeclared AI credentials, local data sent to external AI endpoints, and incomplete/unspecified install steps — so review before installing or run in a sandbox.

dimensions.detail: The code and SKILL.md match the stated purpose (stock quotes, limit-up analysis, portfolio handling). That said, the skill includes AI integration and data-sync scripts (pywencai, akshare, network calls) which are expected for this domain. However the registry metadata declared no required environment variables or primary credential while the code clearly expects AI provider credentials (AI_PROVIDER, AI_API_KEY, AI_MODEL, etc.) — an incoherence that should be explained by the author.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell users to run the bundled backend server and start a frontend. The backend's /api/chat handler builds a context including the user's portfolio/watchlist/stock_codes (from portfolio_data.json and stock_codes.json) and forwards it to external AI provider HTTP endpoints (OpenAI/SiliconFlow/others). That means private portfolio data will be included in network requests to third-party AI services if an AI provider is configured. SKILL.md does not explicitly warn that local portfolio/watchlist data will be transmitted to remote APIs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no registry install spec (instruction-only), but the repository includes scripts/install.sh and backend/requirements.txt. The requirements file does not list key libraries used in the code (e.g., pywencai, pandas, akshare), so the provided 'pip install -r requirements.txt' step is incomplete. The presence of an install script means the skill may modify the environment; you should inspect scripts/install.sh before running. No known malicious remote download URLs were found in the provided manifest.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required env vars, yet backend/AI_CONFIG.md and ai_config.py expect AI_PROVIDER and AI_API_KEY (and optionally AI_BASE_URL, AI_MODEL). The skill will use those credentials to call external AI endpoints, potentially transmitting user portfolio/watchlist context. Requesting AI credentials for chat functionality is reasonable, but the omission from the declared requirements is a mismatch and increases the risk of unnoticed data exfiltration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill stores and modifies local data files (portfolio_data.json, stock_codes.json) and exposes them via local HTTP endpoints. always:false (no forced global inclusion). Writing and reading its own data files is consistent with portfolio management, but because those files contain sensitive user portfolio and notes, running the server exposes them locally and — when AI is enabled — to remote providers. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (disable-model-invocation:false), which is normal; combine that with the above concerns when deciding trust.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing and running this skill:

- Data exfiltration risk: The backend will include local portfolio/watchlist data (portfolio_data.json and stock_codes.json) in context sent to remote AI providers (OpenAI, SiliconFlow, Zhipu, Minimax) if you set AI_PROVIDER/AI_API_KEY. If you enable an AI provider, your personal holdings and notes may be transmitted to third-party servers. If you do not want that, either do not set AI_PROVIDER/AI_API_KEY or set AI_PROVIDER=silence.

- Undeclared environment variables: The registry metadata says 'no required env vars', but the code expects AI_PROVIDER and AI_API_KEY (and possibly AI_BASE_URL / AI_MODEL). The mismatch means automatic deployment tools may not prompt you for necessary secrets. Ask the author to declare required env vars clearly.

- Installation scripts and missing deps: requirements.txt omits libraries used by the code (pywencai, pandas, akshare). Inspect scripts/install.sh before running — run the project in an isolated environment (container, VM) to avoid contaminating your host Python environment. Expect to manually install additional Python packages.

- Local web server exposure: The skill runs a FastAPI server on localhost:8000 by default and serves a frontend. Review CORS and network exposure if you plan to run it on a machine accessible from other hosts. Running the server on a networked machine may expose portfolio endpoints to others.

- Review the code: If you plan to use it, audit these files first: backend/main.py (chat context composition and external calls), backend/ai_service.py (external endpoints used), scripts/install.sh (what it installs), and any file that reads/saves portfolio_data.json. Remove or sanitize portfolio_data.json if you don't want pre-existing sample data uploaded.

- Run safely: If you decide to run it, do so in a sandboxed environment (Docker container or dedicated VM), avoid configuring AI_PROVIDER/AI_API_KEY with production keys until you're confident in the code, and consider using AI_PROVIDER=silence to avoid networked AI calls.

- Ask the publisher: Request the source repository URL, a clear list of required env vars, and a statement about whether /api/chat includes portfolio data in outbound requests. If the author confirms and documents these behaviors, reassess; otherwise treat the skill as requiring caution.
